art.title: Deer in Bloom
art.review: There's something achingly tender about this — the deer's stillness against an explosion of pink petals. The oil texture gives it weight that digital work often lacks.

art.title: Tulip Study
art.review: Jewel-toned and almost baroque in its richness. The layering of reds and pinks against deep black feels dramatic without being overwrought — a perfect still life.

art.title: Sea Angel Trifold
art.review: Infographic design done beautifully — the dark palette and illustrated creatures give it the feel of a museum piece rather than an educational pamphlet. Information and aesthetics in harmony.

art.title: White Lily
art.review: The light source is almost supernatural — petals rendered with such translucency you expect to see your hand through them. Quietly stunning botanical work.

art.title: Spade Fish Print
art.review: Charming vintage-label energy with the stars and nautical typography. The soft blue palette keeps it from feeling kitschy — a nice piece of commercial folk art.

art.title: Abstract Warm Gradient
art.review: The kind of abstract work that rewards staring — amber and rust bleeding into dark violet with a softness that feels almost photographic. Would hang this in a heartbeat.

art.title: Line Tattoo Study
art.review: Tattoo as fine art — the linework is impossibly precise, botanical motifs winding up the arm like something grown rather than drawn. A masterclass in negative space.
